SOURCE: Practice Direction 57 – Probate
SOURCEPAGE: Practice Direction 57
CATEGORY: Civil Procedure Rules and Practice Directions
SECTION: Practice Direction 57
## PRACTICE DIRECTION 57

# PRACTICE DIRECTION 57 – PROBATE

# This Practice Direction supplements Part 57

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 57] Contents of this Practice Direction

## I   PROBATE CLAIMS

## General

## 1.1

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 57 > 1.1] This Section of this practice direction applies to contentious probate claims.

## 1.2

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 57 > 1.2] The rules and procedure relating to non-contentious probate proceedings (also known as ‘common form’) are the Non-Contentious Probate Rules 1987 as amended.

## How to start a probate claim

## 2.1

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 57 > 2.1] A claim form and all subsequent court documents relating to a probate claim must be marked at the top ‘In the estate of [name] deceased (Probate)’.

## 2.2

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 57 > 2.2] The claim form must be issued out of –

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 57 > 2.2] (1) Chancery Chambers at the Royal Courts of Justice; or

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 57 > 2.2] (2) one of the Chancery district registries; or

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 57 > 2.2] (3) if the claim is suitable to be heard in the County Court –

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 57 > 2.2] (a) a County Court hearing centre in a place where there is also a Chancery district registry; or

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 57 > 2.2] (b) the County Court at Central London.

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 57 > 2.2] There are Chancery district registries at Birmingham, Bristol, Caernarfon, Cardiff, Leeds, Liverpool, Manchester, Mold, Newcastle upon Tyne and Preston.

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 57 > 2.2] (Article 2(7B) of the High Court and County Courts Jurisdiction Order 1991 identifies which probate claims may be heard in the County Court.)

## 2.3

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 57 > 2.3] When the claim form is issued, the relevant office will send a notice to Leeds District Probate Registry, Coronet House, Queen Street, Leeds, LS1 2BA, DX 26451 Leeds (Park Square), telephone 0113 243 1505, requesting that all testamentary documents, grants of representation and other relevant documents currently held at any probate registry are sent to the relevant office.

## 2.4

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 57 > 2.4] The commencement of a probate claim will, unless a court otherwise directs, prevent any grant of probate or letters of administration being made until the probate claim has been disposed of.

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 57 > 2.4] (Rule 45 of the Non-Contentious Probate Rules 1987 makes provision for notice of the probate claim to be given, and section 117 of the Senior Courts Act 1981 for the grant of letters of administration pending the determination of a probate claim. Paragraph 8 of this practice direction makes provision about an application for such a grant.)

## Testamentary documents and evidence about testamentary documents

## 3.1

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 57 > 3.1] Unless the court orders otherwise, if a testamentary document is held by the court (whether it was lodged by a party or it was previously held at a probate registry) when the claim has been disposed of the court will send it to the Leeds District Probate Registry.

## 3.2

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 57 > 3.2] The written evidence about testamentary documents required by this Part –

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 57 > 3.2] (1) should be in the form annexed to this practice direction; and

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 57 > 3.2] (2) must be signed by the party personally and not by his solicitor or other representative (except that if the party is a child or protected party the written evidence must be signed by his litigation friend).

## 3.3

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 57 > 3.3] In a case in which there is urgent need to commence a probate claim (for example, in order to be able to apply immediately for the appointment of an administrator pending the determination of the claim) and it is not possible for the claimant to lodge the testamentary documents or to file the evidence about testamentary documents in the relevant office at the same time as the claim form is to be issued, the court may direct that the claimant shall be allowed to issue the claim form upon his giving an undertaking to the court to lodge the documents and file the evidence within such time as the court shall specify.

## Case management

## 4

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 57 > 4] In giving case management directions in a probate claim the court will give consideration to the questions –

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 57 > 4] (1) whether any person who may be affected by the claim and who is not joined as a party should be joined as a party or given notice of the claim, whether under rule 19.8A or otherwise; and

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 57 > 4] (2) whether to make a representation order under rule 19.6 or rule 19.7.

## Summary judgment

## 5.1

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 57 > 5.1] If an order pronouncing for a will in solemn form is sought on an application for summary judgment, the evidence in support of the application must include written evidence proving due execution of the will.

## 5.2

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 57 > 5.2] If a defendant has given notice in his defence under rule 57.7(5) that he raises no positive case but –

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 57 > 5.2] (1) he insists that the will be proved in solemn form; and

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 57 > 5.2] (2) for that purpose he will cross-examine the witnesses who attested the will;

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 57 > 5.2] any application by the claimant for summary judgment is subject to the right of that defendant to require those witnesses to attend court for cross-examination.

## Settlement of a probate claim

## 6.1

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 57 > 6.1] If at any time the parties agree to settle a probate claim, the court may –

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 57 > 6.1] (1) order the trial of the claim on written evidence, which will lead to a grant in solemn form;

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 57 > 6.1] (2) order that the claim be discontinued or dismissed under rule 57.11, which will lead to a grant in common form; or

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 57 > 6.1] (3) pronounce for or against the validity of one or more wills under section 49 of the Administration of Justice Act 1985.

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 57 > 6.1] (For a form of order which is also applicable to discontinuance and which may be adapted as appropriate, see Practice Form No. CH38)

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 57 > 6.1] (Section 49 of the Administration of Justice Act 1985 permits a probate claim to be compromised without a trial if every ‘relevant beneficiary’, as defined in that section, has consented to the proposed order. It is only available in the High Court.)

## 6.2

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 57 > 6.2] Applications under section 49 of the Administration of Justice Act 1985 may be heard by a master or district judge and must be supported by written evidence identifying the relevant beneficiaries and exhibiting the written consent of each of them. The written evidence of testamentary documents required by rule 57.5 will still be necessary.

## Application for an order to bring in a will, etc.

## 7.1

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 57 > 7.1] Any party applying for an order under section 122 of the Senior Courts Act 1981 (‘the 1981 Act’) must serve the application notice on the person against whom the order is sought.

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 57 > 7.1] (Section 122 of the 1981 Act empowers the court to order a person to attend court for examination, and to answer questions and bring in documents, if there are reasonable grounds for believing that such person has knowledge of a testamentary document. Rule 50(1) of the Non-Contentious Probate Rules 1987 makes similar provision where a probate claim has not been commenced.)

## 7.2

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 57 > 7.2] An application for the issue of a witness summons under section 123 of the 1981 Act –

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 57 > 7.2] (1) may be made without notice; and

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 57 > 7.2] (2) must be supported by written evidence setting out the grounds of the application.

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 57 > 7.2] (Section 123 of the 1981 Act empowers the court, where it appears that any person has in his possession, custody or power a testamentary document, to issue a witness summons ordering such person to bring in that document. Rule 50(2) of the Non-Contentious Probate Rules makes similar provision where a probate claim has not been commenced.)

## 7.3

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 57 > 7.3] An application under section 122 or 123 of the 1981 Act should be made to a master or district judge.

## 7.4

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 57 > 7.4] A person against whom a witness summons is issued under section 123 of the 1981 Act who denies that the testamentary document referred to in the witness summons is in his possession or under his control may file written evidence to that effect.

## Administration pending the determination of a probate claim

## 8.1

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 57 > 8.1] An application under section 117 of the Senior Courts Act 1981 for an order for the grant of administration pending the determination of a probate claim should be made by application notice in the probate claim.

## 8.2

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 57 > 8.2] If an order for a grant of administration is made under section 117 of the 1981 Act –

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 57 > 8.2] (1) Rules 69.4 to 69.7 shall apply as if the administrator were a receiver appointed by the court;

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 57 > 8.2] (2) if the court allows the administrator remuneration under rule 69.7, it may make an order under section 117(3) of the 1981 Act assigning the remuneration out of the estate of the deceased; and

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 57 > 8.2] (3) every application relating to the conduct of the administration shall be made by application notice in the probate claim.

## 8.3

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 57 > 8.3] An order under section 117 may be made by a master or district judge.

## 8.4

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 57 > 8.4] If an order is made under section 117 an application for the grant of letters of administration should be made to the Principal Registry of the Family Division, First Avenue House, 42–49 High Holborn, London WC1V 6NP.

## 8.5

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 57 > 8.5] The appointment of an administrator to whom letters of administration are granted following an order under section 117 will cease automatically when a final order in the probate claim is made but will continue pending any appeal.

## II   RECTIFICATION OF WILLS

## Scope of this Section

## 9.

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 57 > 9.] This Section of this practice direction applies to claims for the rectification of a will.

## Lodging the grant

## 10.1

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 57 > 10.1] If the claimant is the person to whom the grant was made in respect of the will of which rectification is sought, he must, unless the court orders otherwise, lodge the probate or letters of administration with the will annexed with the court when the claim form is issued.

## 10.2

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 57 > 10.2] If a defendant has the probate or letters of administration in his possession or under his control, he must, unless the court orders otherwise, lodge it in the relevant office within 14 days after the service of the claim form on him.

## Orders

## 11.

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 57 > 11.] A copy of every order made for the rectification of a will shall be sent to the Principal Registry of the Family Division for filing, and a memorandum of the order shall be endorsed on, or permanently annexed to, the grant under which the estate is administered.

## III   SUBSTITUTION AND REMOVAL OF PERSONAL REPRESENTATIVES

## Scope of this Section

## 12.

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 57 > 12.] This Section of this practice direction applies to claims and applications for substitution or removal of a personal representative. If substitution or removal of a personal representative is sought by application in existing proceedings, this Section shall apply with references to the claim, claim form and claimant being read as if they referred to the application, application notice and applicant respectively.

## Starting the claim

## 13.1

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 57 > 13.1] The claim form must be accompanied by –

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 57 > 13.1] (1) either –

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 57 > 13.1] (a) a sealed or certified copy of the grant of probate or letters of administration, or

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 57 > 13.1] (b) where the claim is to substitute or remove an executor and is made before a grant of probate has been issued, the original or, if the original is not available, a copy of the will; and

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 57 > 13.1] (2) written evidence containing the grounds of the claim and the following information so far as it is known to the claimant –

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 57 > 13.1] (a) brief details of the property comprised in the estate, with an approximate estimate of its capital value and any income that is received from it;

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 57 > 13.1] (b) brief details of the liabilities of the estate;

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 57 > 13.1] (c) the names and addresses of the persons who are in possession of the documents relating to the estate;

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 57 > 13.1] (d) the names of the beneficiaries and their respective interests in the estate; and

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 57 > 13.1] (e) the name, address and occupation of any proposed substituted personal representative.

## 13.2

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 57 > 13.2] If the claim is for the appointment of a substituted personal representative, the claim form must be accompanied by –

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 57 > 13.2] (1) a signed or (in the case of the Public Trustee or a corporation) sealed consent to act; and

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 57 > 13.2] (2) written evidence as to the fitness of the proposed substituted personal representative, if an individual, to act.

## Production of the grant

## 14.1

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 57 > 14.1] On the hearing of the claim the personal representative must produce to the Court the grant of representation to the deceased’s estate.

## 14.2

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 57 > 14.2] If an order is made substituting or removing the personal representative, the grant (together with a sealed copy of the order) must be sent to and remain in the custody of the Principal Registry of the Family Division until a memorandum of the order has been endorsed on or permanently annexed to the grant.

## 14.3

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 57 > 14.3] Where the claim is to substitute or remove an executor and the claim is made before a grant of probate has been issued, paragraphs 14.1 and 14.2 do not apply. Where in such a case an order is made substituting or removing an executor a sealed copy of the order must be sent to the Principal Registry of the Family Division where it will be recorded and retained pending any application for a grant. An order sent to the Principal Registry in accordance with this paragraph must be accompanied by a note of the full name and date of death of the deceased, if it is not apparent on the face of the order.

## IV   CLAIMS UNDER THE INHERITANCE (PROVISION FOR FAMILY AND DEPENDANTS) ACT 1975

## Acknowledgment of service by personal representative – rule 57.16(4)

## 15.

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 57 > 15.] Where a defendant who is a personal representative wishes to remain neutral in relation to the claim, and agrees to abide by any decision which the court may make, he should state this in Section A of the acknowledgment of service form.

## Written evidence of personal representative – rule 57.16(5)

## 16.

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 57 > 16.] The written evidence filed by a defendant who is a personal representative must state to the best of that person’s ability –

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 57 > 16.] (1) full details of the value of the deceased’s net estate, as defined in section 25(1) of the Act;

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 57 > 16.] (2) the person or classes of persons beneficially interested in the estate, and –

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 57 > 16.] (a) the names and (unless they are parties to the claim) addresses of all living beneficiaries; and

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 57 > 16.] (b) the value of their interests in the estate so far as they are known.

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 57 > 16.] (3) whether any living beneficiary (and if so, naming him) is a child or a person who lacks capacity (within the meaning of the Mental Capacity Act 2005); and

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 57 > 16.] (4) any facts which might affect the exercise of the court’s powers under the Act.

## Separate representation of claimants

## 17.

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 57 > 17.] If a claim is made jointly by two or more claimants, and it later appears that any of the claimants have a conflict of interests –

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 57 > 17.] (1) any claimant may choose to be represented at any hearing by separate solicitors or counsel, or may appear in person; and

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 57 > 17.] (2) if the court considers that claimants who are represented by the same solicitors or counsel ought to be separately represented, it may adjourn the application until they are.

## Production of the grant

## 18.1

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 57 > 18.1] On the hearing of a claim the personal representative must produce to the court the original grant of representation to the deceased’s estate.

## 18.2

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 57 > 18.2] If the court makes an order under the Act, the original grant (together with a sealed copy of the order) must be sent to the Principal Registry of the Family Division for a memorandum of the order to be endorsed on or permanently annexed to the grant in accordance with section 19(3) of the Act.

## 18.3

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 57 > 18.3] Every final order embodying terms of compromise made in proceedings under the Act, whether made with or without a hearing, must contain a direction that a memorandum of the order shall be endorsed on or permanently annexed to the probate or letters of administration and a copy of the order shall be sent to the Principal Registry of the Family Division with the relevant grant of probate or letters of administration for endorsement.

## ANNEX

## A form of witness statement or affidavit about testamentary documents

## (CPR rule 57.5)

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 57 > (CPR rule 57.5)] (Title of the claim)

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 57 > (CPR rule 57.5)] I [name and address] the claimant/defendant in this claim state [on oath] that I have no knowledge of any document –

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 57 > (CPR rule 57.5)] (i) being or purported to be or having the form or effect of a will or codicil of [name of deceased] whose estate is the subject of this claim;

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 57 > (CPR rule 57.5)] (ii) being or purporting to be a draft or written instructions for any such will or codicil made by or at the request of or under the instructions of the deceased;

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 57 > (CPR rule 57.5)] (iii) being or purporting to be evidence of the contents or a copy of any such will or codicil which is alleged to have been lost or destroyed,

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 57 > (CPR rule 57.5)] except … [describe any testamentary document of the deceased, and if any such document is not in your control, give the name and address of the person who you believe has possession or control of it, or state that you do not know the name and address of that person] …

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 57 > (CPR rule 57.5)] [I believe that the facts stated in this witness statement are true. I understand that proceedings for contempt of court may be brought against anyone who makes, or causes to be made, a false statement in a document verified by a statement of truth without an honest belief in its truth.] [or jurat for affidavit]

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 57 > (CPR rule 57.5)] (NOTE: ‘testamentary document’ is defined in CPR rule 57.1)

[This Practice Direction supplements Part 57 > (CPR rule 57.5)] Updated: Thursday, 6 April 2023

SOURCE: Practice Direction 61 – Admiralty Claims
SOURCEPAGE: Practice Direction 61
CATEGORY: Civil Procedure Rules and Practice Directions
SECTION: Practice Direction 61
## Part 2

Document: Practice Direction 61
Section: 10.4 An acknowledgment of service in a limitation claim must be in form ADM16B.
Part 2 of 2
==================================================
## 10.4 An acknowledgment of service in a limitation claim must be in form ADM16B.

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.4 An acknowledgment of service in a limitation claim must be in form ADM16B.] 10.5 An application for a restricted limitation decree must be in form ADM17 and the decree issued by the court on such an application must be in form ADM18.

## 10.6 An application for a general limitation decree must be in form ADM17A.

## 10.7 Where –

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.7 Where –] (1) the right to limit is not admitted; and

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.7 Where –] (2) the claimant seeks a general limitation decree in form ADM17A,

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.7 Where –] the claimant must, within 7 days after the date of the filing of the defence of the defendant last served or the expiry of the time for doing so, apply for an appointment before the Registrar for a case management conference.

## 10.8 On an application under rule 61.11(12) the Registrar may –

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.8 On an application under rule 61.11(12) the Registrar may –] (1) grant a general limitation decree; or

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.8 On an application under rule 61.11(12) the Registrar may –] (2) if he does not grant a decree –

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.8 On an application under rule 61.11(12) the Registrar may –] (a) order service of a defence; and

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.8 On an application under rule 61.11(12) the Registrar may –] (c) make such other case management directions as may be appropriate.

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.8 On an application under rule 61.11(12) the Registrar may –] 10.9 The fact that a limitation fund has lapsed under rule 61.11(20)(a) does not prevent the establishment of a new fund.

## 10.9A A limitation fund may be constituted by—

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.9A A limitation fund may be constituted by—] (1) making a payment into court;

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.9A A limitation fund may be constituted by—] (2) providing court-approved security; or

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.9A A limitation fund may be constituted by—] (3) a combination of (1) and (2).

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.9A A limitation fund may be constituted by—] 10.10 Where a limitation fund is established by making a payment into court, the sum paid in must be –

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.9A A limitation fund may be constituted by—] (1) the sterling equivalent of the number of special drawing rights to which [the claimant] claims to be entitled to limit his liability under the Merchant Shipping Act 1995; together with

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.9A A limitation fund may be constituted by—] (2) interest from the date of the occurrence giving rise to his liability to the date of payment into court.

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.9A A limitation fund may be constituted by—] 10.11 Where the claimant does not know the sterling equivalent referred to in paragraph 10.10(1) on the date of payment into court he may –

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.9A A limitation fund may be constituted by—] (1) calculate it on the basis of the latest available published sterling equivalent of a special drawing right as fixed by the International Monetary Fund; and

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.9A A limitation fund may be constituted by—] (2) in the event of the sterling equivalent of a special drawing right on the date of payment into court being different from that used for calculating the amount of that payment into court the claimant may –

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.9A A limitation fund may be constituted by—] (a) make up any deficiency by making a further payment into court which, if made within 14 days after the payment into court, will be treated, except for the purpose of the rules relating to the accrual of interest on money paid into court, as if made on the date of that payment into court; or

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.9A A limitation fund may be constituted by—] (b) apply to the court for payment out of any excess amount (together with any interest accrued) paid into court.

## 10.12 An application under paragraph 10.11(2)(b) –

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.12 An application under paragraph 10.11(2)(b) –] (1) may be made without notice; and

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.12 An application under paragraph 10.11(2)(b) –] (2) must be supported by evidence proving, to the satisfaction of the court, the sterling equivalent of the appropriate number of special drawing rights on the date of payment into court.

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.12 An application under paragraph 10.11(2)(b) –] 10.13 The claimant must give notice in writing to every defendant and interested party whose address the claimant knows, of –

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.12 An application under paragraph 10.11(2)(b) –] (1) any payment into court specifying –

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.12 An application under paragraph 10.11(2)(b) –] (a) the date of the payment in;

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.12 An application under paragraph 10.11(2)(b) –] (b) the amount paid in and how it has been calculated;

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.12 An application under paragraph 10.11(2)(b) –] (c) the amount and rate of interest included; and

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.12 An application under paragraph 10.11(2)(b) –] (d) the period to which it relates; and

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.12 An application under paragraph 10.11(2)(b) –] (2) any excess amount (and interest) paid out to him under paragraph 10.11(2)(b).

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.12 An application under paragraph 10.11(2)(b) –] 10.13A Where a claimant wishes to establish a limitation fund (in whole or in part) by providing security, the claimant must apply to the court for an order approving the security.  The application may be made on paper and without notice, but the applicant should first seek to agree the provider, form, nature, and terms of the proposed security with any named defendant and any interested party before making the application (unless the circumstances of the case make that impracticable).

## 10.13B An application under paragraph 10.13A must be –

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.13B An application under paragraph 10.13A must be –] (1) accompanied by the proposed security or a draft thereof; and

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.13B An application under paragraph 10.13A must be –] (2) supported by evidence of—

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.13B An application under paragraph 10.13A must be –] (a) the adequacy of the proposed security; and

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.13B An application under paragraph 10.13A must be –] (b) if the proposed security is expressed in sterling, the sterling equivalent of the appropriate number of special drawing rights on the date the application is made.

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.13B An application under paragraph 10.13A must be –] 10.13C The court shall approve the proposed security if it is satisfied that it is adequate in all the circumstances (including its form, nature, terms, and the financial standing of the person offering it).

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.13B An application under paragraph 10.13A must be –] 10.13D Where a limitation fund is established (in whole or in part) by providing court-approved security, the security may be expressed in special drawing rights or sterling. If the security is expressed in sterling, the amount of the security shall be the same as if the fund were being constituted by payment in to court and paragraphs 10.10 and 10.11(1) above shall apply in an equivalent sense.

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.13B An application under paragraph 10.13A must be –] 10.13E The claimant must give notice in writing to every named defendant and any interested party whose address is known of any court-approved security lodged at court, specifying—

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.13B An application under paragraph 10.13A must be –] (1) the terms of the security;

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.13B An application under paragraph 10.13A must be –] (2) the date on which the security was lodged at court;

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.13B An application under paragraph 10.13A must be –] (3) how the amount of security was calculated;

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.13B An application under paragraph 10.13A must be –] (4) the amount and rate of interest included, and the period to which it relates,

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.13B An application under paragraph 10.13A must be –] and shall provide on request any person so notified with a copy of the security so lodged and the application made under paragraph 10.13A.

## 10.13F An application to set aside the court’s approval of a security may be made by—

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.13F An application to set aside the court’s approval of a security may be made by—] (1) any person (whether a defendant, an interested party or another), who was not given notice of the claimant’s application under paragraph 10.13A; or

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.13F An application to set aside the court’s approval of a security may be made by—] (2) any person (whether a defendant, an interested party or another) if circumstances relevant to the adequacy of the security have changed since it was approved by the court.

## 10.13G An application under paragraph 10.13F(1) must be –

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.13G An application under paragraph 10.13F(1) must be –] (1) made on notice to the provider of the security, all claimants, all named defendants, and all interested parties (whose addresses are known);

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.13G An application under paragraph 10.13F(1) must be –] (2) supported by evidence setting out the reasons why the court’s approval of the security should be set aside; and

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.13G An application under paragraph 10.13F(1) must be –] (3) made within 21 days of receipt by the applicant of notice given under paragraph 10.13E (if such notice was given to the applicant) or as soon as reasonably practicable (if no such notice was given to the applicant).

## 10.13H An application under paragraph 10.13F(2) must be—

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.13H An application under paragraph 10.13F(2) must be—] (1) made on notice to the provider of the security, all claimants, all named defendants, and all Interested Parties (whose addresses are known);

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.13H An application under paragraph 10.13F(2) must be—] (2) supported by evidence setting out the change in circumstances justifying the setting aside of the court’s approval of the security; and

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.13H An application under paragraph 10.13F(2) must be—] (3) made as soon as reasonably practicable after discovery of the change of circumstances.

## 10.13I On an application under paragraph 10.13F, the court may—

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.13I On an application under paragraph 10.13F, the court may—] (1) confirm its approval of the adequacy of the security;

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.13I On an application under paragraph 10.13F, the court may—] (2) set aside its approval of the adequacy of the security; and/or

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.13I On an application under paragraph 10.13F, the court may—] (3) require the fund to be reconstituted in such manner and on such terms as it thinks fit.

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.13I On an application under paragraph 10.13F, the court may—] 10.13J If a claimant has constituted a fund by payment in of money, it may apply at any time for an order permitting the reconstitution of the fund (in whole or in part) by means of a court-approved security. Any such application shall be made in accordance with paragraphs 10.13A to 10.13E, and paragraphs 10.13F to 10.13I shall apply to any order made.”.

## 10.14 A claim against the fund must be in form ADM20 .

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.14 A claim against the fund must be in form ADM20 .] 10.15 A defendant’s statement of case filed and served in accordance with rule 61.11(15) must contain particulars of the defendant’s claim.

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.14 A claim against the fund must be in form ADM20 .] 10.16 Any defendant who is unable to file and serve a statement of case in accordance with rule 61.11(15) and paragraph 10.15 must file a declaration, verified by a statement of truth, in form ADM21 stating the reason for his inability.

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.14 A claim against the fund must be in form ADM20 .] 10.17 No later than 7 days after the time for filing claims [or declarations], the Registrar will fix a date for a case management conference at which directions will be given for the further conduct of the proceedings.

## 10.18 Nothing in rule 61.11 prevents limitation being relied on by way of defence.

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.18 Nothing in rule 61.11 prevents limitation being relied on by way of defence.] 11.1 For the purposes of section 177 of the Merchant Shipping Act 1995 (‘the Act’), the Fund may be given notice of proceedings by any party to a claim against an owner or guarantor in respect of liability under section 153 of the Act by that person serving a notice in writing on the Fund together with copies of the claim form and any statements of case served in the claim.

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.18 Nothing in rule 61.11 prevents limitation being relied on by way of defence.] 11.2 Notice given to the Fund under paragraph 11.1 shall be deemed to have been given to the Supplementary Fund.

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.18 Nothing in rule 61.11 prevents limitation being relied on by way of defence.] 11.3 The Fund or the Supplementary Fund may intervene in any claim to which paragraph 11.1 applies, (whether or not served with the notice), by serving notice of intervention on the –

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.18 Nothing in rule 61.11 prevents limitation being relied on by way of defence.] (1) owner;

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.18 Nothing in rule 61.11 prevents limitation being relied on by way of defence.] (2) guarantor; and

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 10.18 Nothing in rule 61.11 prevents limitation being relied on by way of defence.] (3) court.

## 11.4 Where a judgment is given against –

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 11.4 Where a judgment is given against –] (1) the Fund in any claim under section 175 of the Act;

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 11.4 Where a judgment is given against –] (2) the Supplementary Fund in any claim under section 176A of the Act, the Registrar will arrange for a stamped copy of the judgment to be sent by post to –

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 11.4 Where a judgment is given against –] (a) the Fund (where paragraph (1) applies);

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 11.4 Where a judgment is given against –] (b) the Supplementary Fund (where paragraph (2) applies).

## 11.5 Notice to the Registrar of the matters set out in –

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 11.5 Notice to the Registrar of the matters set out in –] (1) section 176(3)(b) of the Act in proceedings under section 175; or

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 11.5 Notice to the Registrar of the matters set out in –] (2) section 176B(2)(b) of the Act in proceedings under section 176A, must be given in writing and sent to the court by –

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 11.5 Notice to the Registrar of the matters set out in –] (a) the Fund (where paragraph (1) applies);

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 11.5 Notice to the Registrar of the matters set out in –] (b) the Supplementary Fund (where paragraph (2) applies).

## References to the Registrar

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > References to the Registrar] 13.1 The court may at any stage in the claim refer any question or issue for determination by the Registrar (a ‘reference’).

## 13.2 Unless the court orders otherwise, where a reference has been ordered –

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 13.2 Unless the court orders otherwise, where a reference has been ordered –] (1) if particulars of claim have not already been served, the claimant must file and serve particulars of claim on all other parties within 14 days after the date of the order;

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 13.2 Unless the court orders otherwise, where a reference has been ordered –] (2) any party opposing the claim must file a defence to the claim within 14 days after service of the particulars of claim on him;

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 13.2 Unless the court orders otherwise, where a reference has been ordered –] (3) the rules concerning statements of case shall apply to the particulars of claim, the defence and any other statements of case served in the reference; and

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 13.2 Unless the court orders otherwise, where a reference has been ordered –] (4) all documents which the claimant (or counterclaimant) in a reference intends to rely on in order to show that the sums claimed were properly incurred and paid (‘vouchers’) shall be appended to their first statement of case in the reference and cross referenced to the sums being claimed, unless there is a compelling reason not to do so.

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > 13.2 Unless the court orders otherwise, where a reference has been ordered –] 13.3 Within 7 days after the defence is filed, the claimant must apply for an appointment before the Registrar for a case management conference.

## Undertakings

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > Undertakings] 14.1 Where, in or this practice direction, any undertaking to the Marshal is required it must be given –

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > Undertakings] (1) in writing and to his satisfaction; or

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > Undertakings] (2) in accordance with such other arrangements as he may require.

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > Undertakings] 14.2 Where any party is dissatisfied with a direction given by the Marshal in this respect he may apply to the Registrar for a ruling.

## Admiralty Claims

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > Admiralty Claims] Admiralty forms – GOV.UK (opens in a new tab)

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > Admiralty Claims] Available on the forms page.

[This Practice Direction Supplements CPR Part 61 > Admiralty Claims] Updated: Sunday, 1 October 2023

SOURCEPAGE: Practice Direction 70A
CATEGORY: Civil Procedure Rules and Practice Directions

## PRACTICE DIRECTION 70A

# PRACTICE DIRECTION 70A – ENFORCEMENT OF JUDGMENTS AND ORDERS

part70#id4541512

# This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89.

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89.] Contents of this Practice Direction

## SECTION I – GENERAL

## Definitions

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > Definitions] A1.1 In this Practice Direction—

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > Definitions] (1) ‘writ of control’ is to be construed in accordance with section 62(4) of the Tribunals Courts and Enforcement Act 2007;

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > Definitions] (2) ‘writ of execution’ includes-

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > Definitions] (a) a writ of possession;

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > Definitions] (b) a writ of delivery;

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > Definitions] (c) a writ of sequestration;

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > Definitions] (d) a writ of fieri facias de bonis ecclesiasticis,

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > Definitions] and any further writ in aid of any such writs, but does not include a writ of control.

## Methods of enforcing money judgments – rule 70.2

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > Methods of enforcing money judgments – rule 70.2] 1.1 A judgment creditor may enforce a judgment or order for the payment of money by any of the following methods:

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > Methods of enforcing money judgments – rule 70.2] (1) a writ of control or warrant of control (see Parts 83 and 84);

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > Methods of enforcing money judgments – rule 70.2] (2) a third party debt order (see Part 72);

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > Methods of enforcing money judgments – rule 70.2] (3) a charging order, stop order or stop notice (see Part 73);

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > Methods of enforcing money judgments – rule 70.2] (4) in the County Court, an attachment of earnings order (see Part 89);

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > Methods of enforcing money judgments – rule 70.2] (5) the appointment of a receiver (see Part 69).

## 1.2 In addition the court may make the following orders against a judgment debtor –

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > 1.2 In addition the court may make the following orders against a judgment debtor –] (1) an order in contempt proceedings under Part 81, but only if the debtor is found in contempt of court; and

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > 1.2 In addition the court may make the following orders against a judgment debtor –] (2) in the High Court, a writ of sequestration in an application under Part 83.

## 1.3 The enforcement of a judgment or order may be affected by –

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > 1.3 The enforcement of a judgment or order may be affected by –] (1) the enactments relating to insolvency; and

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > 1.3 The enforcement of a judgment or order may be affected by –] (2) County Court administration orders.

## Proceedings for enforcement in the County Court – rule 70.3

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > Proceedings for enforcement in the County Court – rule 70.3] 2.1 An application to enforce a judgment in the County Court may be made an any County Court hearing centre, unless an enactment, rule or practice direction provides otherwise.

## 2.2 Omitted

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > 2.2 Omitted] 2.3 If for any reason proceedings for the enforcement of a judgment are transferred, the court will give notice of the transfer to all the parties.

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > 2.2 Omitted] 2.4 When the proceedings have been transferred, the parties must take any further steps in the proceedings in the court to which they have been transferred, unless a rule or practice direction provides otherwise.

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > 2.2 Omitted] (Part 52 and Practice Directions 52A and 52B provide to which court or judge an appeal against the judgment or order, or an application for permission to appeal, must be made.)

## Enforcement of High Court judgment or order in the County Court – rule 70.3

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > Enforcement of High Court judgment or order in the County Court – rule 70.3] 3.1 If a judgment creditor wishes to enforce a High Court judgment or order in the County Court, they must file the following documents in the County Court with the application notice or request for enforcement–

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > Enforcement of High Court judgment or order in the County Court – rule 70.3] (1) a copy of the judgment or order;

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > Enforcement of High Court judgment or order in the County Court – rule 70.3] (2) a certificate verifying the amount due under the judgment or order;

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > Enforcement of High Court judgment or order in the County Court – rule 70.3] (3) if a writ of execution or writ of control has previously been issued in the High Court to enforce the judgment or order, a copy of the relevant enforcement officer’s return to the writ; and

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > Enforcement of High Court judgment or order in the County Court – rule 70.3] (4) a copy of the order transferring the proceedings to the County Court.

## 3.2 In this paragraph and paragraph 7 –

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > 3.2 In this paragraph and paragraph 7 –] (1) ‘enforcement officer’ means an individual who is authorised to act as an enforcement officer under the Courts Act 2003; and

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > 3.2 In this paragraph and paragraph 7 –] (2) ‘relevant enforcement officer’ means –

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > 3.2 In this paragraph and paragraph 7 –] (a) in relation to a writ of execution or writ of control which is directed to a single enforcement officer, that officer;

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > 3.2 In this paragraph and paragraph 7 –] (b) in relation to a writ of execution or writ of control which is directed to two or more enforcement officers, the officer to whom the writ is allocated.

## 4.1 The information referred to in rule 70.5(2A) must–

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > 4.1 The information referred to in rule 70.5(2A) must–] (a) be included in practice form N322B or, where paragraph 4.1A applies, in the practice form required by paragraph 4.1A(2);

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > 4.1 The information referred to in rule 70.5(2A) must–] (b) specify the statutory provision under which enforcement or the recovery of a sum of money is sought;

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > 4.1 The information referred to in rule 70.5(2A) must–] (c) state the name and address of the person against whom enforcement or recovery is sought;

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > 4.1 The information referred to in rule 70.5(2A) must–] (d) where the decision or compromise requires that person to pay a sum of money, state the amount which remains unpaid; and

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > 4.1 The information referred to in rule 70.5(2A) must–] (e) confirm that, where a sum of money is being recovered pursuant to a compromise, the compromise is not a conditional compromise.

## 4.1A

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > 4.1A] (1) This paragraph applies where–

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > 4.1A] (a) either –

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > 4.1A] (i) the decision to be enforced is a decision of an employment tribunal in England and Wales; or

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > 4.1A] (ii) the application is for the recovery of a compromise sum under section 19A(3) of the Employment Tribunals Act 1996; and

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > 4.1A] (b) the party seeking to enforce the decision wishes to enforce by way of a writ of control

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > 4.1A] (2) The practice form which is to be used is–

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > 4.1A] (a) where paragraph (1)(a)(i) applies, practice form N471;

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > 4.1A] (b) where paragraph (1)(a)(ii) applies, practice form N471A.

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > 4.1A] 4.2 An application under rule 70.5(3) for an order to enforce a decision or compromise must be made by filing an application notice in practice form N322A.

## 4.3 The application notice must state –

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > 4.3 The application notice must state –] (a) the name and address of the person against whom the order is sought;

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > 4.3 The application notice must state –] (b) how much remains unpaid or what obligation remains to be performed; and

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > 4.3 The application notice must state –] (c) where the application relates to a conditional compromise, details of what under the compromise the applicant is required to do and has done under the compromise in addition to discontinuing or not starting proceedings.

## 4.4 Where –

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > 4.4 Where –] (a) the application relates to a conditional compromise; and

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > 4.4 Where –] (b) the application notice is served by the applicant on the respondent,

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > 4.4 Where –] the applicant must file a certificate of service with the court within 7 days of service of the application notice.

## Registration of decisions in the High Court for enforcement – rule 70.5(8)

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > Registration of decisions in the High Court for enforcement – rule 70.5(8)] 5.1 An application to the High Court under an enactment to register a decision for enforcement must be made in writing to the head clerk of the Action Department at the Royal Courts of Justice, Strand, London WC2A 2LL.

## 5.2 The application must –

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > 5.2 The application must –] (1) specify the statutory provision under which the application is made;

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > 5.2 The application must –] (2) state the name and address of the person against whom it is sought to enforce the decision;

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > 5.2 The application must –] (3) if the decision requires that person to pay a sum of money, state the amount which remains unpaid.

## Interest on judgment debts

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > Interest on judgment debts] 6 If a judgment creditor is claiming interest on a judgment debt, he must include in his application or request to issue enforcement proceedings in relation to that judgment details of –

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > Interest on judgment debts] (1) the amount of interest claimed and the sum on which it is claimed;

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > Interest on judgment debts] (2) the dates from and to which interest has accrued; and

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > Interest on judgment debts] (3) the rate of interest which has been applied and, where more than one rate of interest has been applied, the relevant dates and rates.

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > Interest on judgment debts] (Interest may be claimed on High Court judgment debts under section 17 of the Judgments Act 1838. The County Courts (Interest on Judgment Debts) Order 1991 specifies when interest may be claimed on the County Court judgment debts.)

## Enforcing a judgment or order against a partnership

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > Enforcing a judgment or order against a partnership] 6A.1 A judgment or order made against a partnership may be enforced against any property of the partnership within the jurisdiction.

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > Enforcing a judgment or order against a partnership] 6A.2 Subject to paragraph 6A.3, a judgment or order made against a partnership may be enforced against any person who is not a limited partner and who –

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > Enforcing a judgment or order against a partnership] (1) acknowledged service of the claim form as a partner;

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > Enforcing a judgment or order against a partnership] (2) having been served as a partner with the claim form, failed to acknowledge service of it;

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > Enforcing a judgment or order against a partnership] (3) admitted in his statement of case that he is or was a partner at a material time; or

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > Enforcing a judgment or order against a partnership] (4) was found by the court to have been a partner at a material time.

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > Enforcing a judgment or order against a partnership] 6A.3 A judgment or order made against a partnership may not be enforced against a limited partner or a member of the partnership who was ordinarily resident outside the jurisdiction when the claim form was issued unless that partner or member–

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > Enforcing a judgment or order against a partnership] (1) acknowledged service of the claim form as a partner;

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > Enforcing a judgment or order against a partnership] (2) was served within the jurisdiction with the claim form as a partner; or

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > Enforcing a judgment or order against a partnership] (3) was served out of the jurisdiction with the claim form, as a partner, with the permission of the court given under Section IV of Part 6.

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > Enforcing a judgment or order against a partnership] 6A.4 A judgment creditor wishing to enforce a judgment or order against a person in circumstances not set out in paragraphs 6A.2 or 6A.3 must apply to the court for permission to enforce the judgment or order.

## Payment of debt after issue of enforcement proceedings

## 7.1 If a judgment debt or part of it is paid –

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > 7.1 If a judgment debt or part of it is paid –] (1) after the judgment creditor has issued any application or request to enforce it; but

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > 7.1 If a judgment debt or part of it is paid –] (2) before –

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > 7.1 If a judgment debt or part of it is paid –] (a) any writ or warrant has been executed; or

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > 7.1 If a judgment debt or part of it is paid –] (b) in any other case, the date fixed for the hearing of the application;

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > 7.1 If a judgment debt or part of it is paid –] the judgment creditor must, unless paragraph 7.2 applies, immediately notify the court in writing.

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > 7.1 If a judgment debt or part of it is paid –] 7.2 If a judgment debt or part of it is paid after the judgment creditor has applied to the High Court for a writ of execution or writ of control, paragraph 7.1 does not apply, and the judgment creditor must instead immediately notify the relevant enforcement officer in writing.

## SECTION II – ENFORCEMENT PROCEEDINGS IN THE CIVIL NATIONAL BUSINESS CENTRE

## Scope

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > Scope] 8.1 This section applies to applications for orders to obtain information from judgment debtors and applications for enforcement of judgments made at the Civil National Business Centre where the proceedings have not been transferred or sent to a County Court hearing centre.

## Applications under Parts 71 and 72

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > Applications under Parts 71 and 72] 9.1 Where an application is made to which rule 71.2(2)(b)(ii) or 72.3(1)(b)(ii) applies, it must be filed at the County Court hearing centre for the district in which the judgment debtor resides or carries on business.

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > Applications under Parts 71 and 72] Paragraphs 10.1 and 10.2 omitted.

## Transfer

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > Transfer] 11.1 Unless the court is satisfied that the application does not comply with the Rules, it will transfer the proceedings to the hearing centre where the application was filed and a court officer will inform the Civil National Business Centre of the transfer.

[This Practice Direction supplements Parts 70, 71, 72, 73 and 89. > Transfer] Updated: Thursday, 10 August 2023

## PRACTICE DIRECTION 77

# PRACTICE DIRECTION 77 – APPLICATIONS FOR AND RELATING TO SERIOUS CRIME PREVENTION ORDERS AND REFERRAL OF RELEASE DECISIONS

# This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 77

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 77] Contents of this Practice Direction

## SECTION 1 – SERIOUS CRIME PREVENTION ORDERS

## Claim form – application for a SCPO

## 1.1

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 77 > 1.1] An application for a SCPO must be started by way of a Part 8 claim form, although the court may decide during the proceedings that it would be more appropriate to continue the proceedings in accordance with Part 7.

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 77 > 1.1] (Rule 8.1(3) allows the court to make an order that the claim continue as if the claimant had not used the Part 8 procedure.)

## 1.2

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 77 > 1.2] The claim form must –

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 77 > 1.2] (1) identify which provisions of section 2(1) of the 2007 Act the applicant relies on and under each provision identified, set out the details of the allegations that the respondent has been involved in serious crime (whether in England and Wales or elsewhere);

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 77 > 1.2] (2) set out the applicant’s grounds for contending that the proposed terms of the SCPO are appropriate for the purpose of protecting the public in accordance with section 1(3) of the 2007 Act; and

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 77 > 1.2] (3) include details of any third party whom the applicant believes is likely to be significantly adversely affected by the SCPO and the nature of that adverse effect.

## 1.3

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 77 > 1.3] The claim form must be accompanied by a draft of the SCPO for which the application is made. The terms of the draft SCPO must include any proposed dates, including those upon which the applicant proposes that the SCPO should come into force and cease to be in force.

## 1.4

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 77 > 1.4] Where it is alleged that the respondent has committed a serious offence, the claim form must be accompanied by evidence that the respondent has been convicted of the offence. Where a certificate of conviction can be obtained, this must be put in evidence.

## 1.5

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 77 > 1.5] Where it is alleged that the respondent has been convicted of an offence in another jurisdiction, the applicant must put in evidence –

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 77 > 1.5] (a) a document from the appropriate public authority in the jurisdiction concerned certifying that the respondent has after due process of law been convicted of the offence; and

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 77 > 1.5] (b) where the document is not in English, a translation of that document into English –

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 77 > 1.5] (i) certified by a notary public or other qualified person; or

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 77 > 1.5] (ii) accompanied by written evidence confirming that the translation is accurate.

## Applications by third parties to make representations

## 2.1

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 77 > 2.1] The evidence in support of an application made under section 9 of the 2007 Act must contain details of why the third party believes the proposed order would be likely to have a significant adverse effect on that third party.

## Application to vary or discharge a SCPO

## 3.1

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 77 > 3.1] The application notice or claim form must contain –

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 77 > 3.1] (1) where the applicant is the person who is the subject of the SCPO, details of the change of circumstances affecting the SCPO;

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 77 > 3.1] (2) where the applicant seeks to vary the SCPO, any grounds advanced by the applicant for contending that the terms of the SCPO as varied would protect the public in accordance with section 17(1) of the 2007 Act;

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 77 > 3.1] (2A) where the applicant for the SCPO seeks to vary the SCPO –

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 77 > 3.1] (a) details of any third party whom the applicant believes is likely to be significantly adversely affected by the proposed variation to the SCPO; and

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 77 > 3.1] (b) details of the nature of that adverse effect;

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 77 > 3.1] (3) where the applicant seeks to vary the SCPO and is a third party or the person who is the subject of the SCPO –

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 77 > 3.1] (a) particulars of why the applicant believes the applicant is significantly adversely affected by the SCPO;

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 77 > 3.1] (b) particulars of how condition A or B in section 17 of the 2007 Act is met; and

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 77 > 3.1] (c) particulars relied upon to establish that the purpose of the application is not to make the SCPO more onerous on the person who is the subject of the order; and

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 77 > 3.1] (4) where the application is for the discharge of the SCPO and the applicant is a third party or the person who is the subject of the SCPO, particulars of –

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 77 > 3.1] (a) why the applicant believes the applicant is significantly adversely affected by the SCPO; and

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 77 > 3.1] (b) how condition A or B in section 18 of the 2007 Act is met.

## 3.2

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 77 > 3.2] Where the application is to vary or discharge a SCPO made by the Crown Court, the claim form must be accompanied by a copy of the SCPO made by the Crown Court.

## Where to make an application

## 4.1

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 77 > 4.1] An application for an SCPO or relating to an SCPO must be filed in the Administrative Court at the Royal Courts of Justice.

## SECTION 3 – REFERRAL OF RELEASE DECISIONS

## Where to make an application

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 77 > Where to make an application] 5.1 Any application concerning the referral of a release decision must be filed in the Administrative Court at the Royal Courts of Justice.

## Victim personal statements

## 6.1 —(1) The court may allow the victim personal statement (VPS) to be read in court—

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 77 > 6.1 —(1) The court may allow the victim personal statement (VPS) to be read in court—] by the maker of the VPS or another person;

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 77 > 6.1 —(1) The court may allow the victim personal statement (VPS) to be read in court—] in whole or in part or in a summary; or

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 77 > 6.1 —(1) The court may allow the victim personal statement (VPS) to be read in court—] in person or through a video link or recording or by some other means,

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 77 > 6.1 —(1) The court may allow the victim personal statement (VPS) to be read in court—] having had regard to—

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 77 > 6.1 —(1) The court may allow the victim personal statement (VPS) to be read in court—] the wishes of the maker of the VPS;

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 77 > 6.1 —(1) The court may allow the victim personal statement (VPS) to be read in court—] the contents of the VPS; and

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 77 > 6.1 —(1) The court may allow the victim personal statement (VPS) to be read in court—] the potential for any harm to the victim or any other person which may arise from the VPS being read in court.

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 77 > 6.1 —(1) The court may allow the victim personal statement (VPS) to be read in court—] (2) Where a VPS is read in court under paragraph (1), neither the maker nor the reader shall be cross-examined on it.

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 77 > 6.1 —(1) The court may allow the victim personal statement (VPS) to be read in court—] (3) Practice Direction 1A applies to any person referred to in this paragraph.

## Licence conditions

## 7.1

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 77 > 7.1] If the court makes an order requiring the applicant to give effect to the Parole Board’s direction to release the prisoner on licence, before deciding whether to include directions as to the conditions to be included in the respondent’s licence on release, the court shall have regard to the guidance in the Ministry of Justice’s and His Majesty’s Prison and Probation Service’s Licence Conditions Policy Framework: Licence conditions policy framework – GOV.UK (opens in a new tab) .

[This Practice Direction supplements CPR Part 77 > 7.1] Updated: Tuesday, 7 February 2023
